prompts: Use case: stylized-concept / technical costume turnaround. Reference image 1 is the approved overall mood and cloak silhouette. Produce ONE high-resolution LANDSCAPE modeler-facing ORTHOGRAPHIC THREE-VIEW SHEET of this cloak alone, with FRONT, RIGHT SIDE, BACK arranged left-to-right, identical scale, aligned neck openings and lowest tips, generous separation. No perspective in the three main views. Neutral pale warm-gray background and restrained studio illumination. No wearer, mannequin, head, arms, torso, clothes, shoes, stand or weapons. All three views must depict exactly the SAME physically buildable garment with matching panel boundaries, feather tiers and asymmetry. Short shoulder fall on anatomical RIGHT (front image left); longest trailing feather fan on anatomical RIGHT (back image right). Not mirrored between views. Keep the approved scarf-wrapped neckline, charcoal weathered fabric, asymmetrical broad cape, subtle copper scorch traces and ember feather tips. IMPORTANT USER CORRECTION: upper cloak is overlapping LAYERS OF CLOTH; lower half is a real STACK OF INDIVIDUAL FEATHERS, not ripped triangular fabric lobes or a single sheet cut into four points. Each feather has a central flexible quill/rib, tapered vanes with delicate barbs, a narrow root buried under the previous tier, and an independently readable free tip. Feathers are soft charcoal-black phoenix feathers, NOT metal armor scales, not gigantic bird wings. Exactly THREE staggered shingled feather tiers: F1 18 short covert feathers 14–20 cm; F2 14 medium feathers 24–34 cm; F3 10 long terminal feathers 32–52 cm, including a few longer irregular trailing feathers on the right. Adjacent feathers overlap about one third to one half width; each lower tier's attachment roots are hidden behind the tier above, feather axes sweep downwards and slightly outward from the right shoulder load path. Buildable top structure: C0 hidden soft textile shoulder/neck support yoke; C1 ONE soft scarf band folded into three uneven draped ridges, not three separate tubes and no rigid standing collar; C2 inner continuous back cloth from upper back down behind feather roots, ending above the longest feather tips; C3 separate asymmetrical outer shoulder shawl with a diagonal front edge over right shoulder, overlapping the upper back cloth and covering the highest feather attachment row. There are clearly TWO back cloth layers C2 and C3, not five arbitrary curtains. Neck wrap opens via a concealed fabric tie under front-left overlap, no visible metal buckle. For 1.73m character: total garment neck-to-lowest-tip approximately 1.30m, maximum rear spread about .68m. Feather transition begins around .50–.60m below neckline. Keep this exact scale and construction in every view. Main views must show DARK FEATHER GEOMETRY clearly: very restrained orange embers only along final vane edges, no large bloom, no fire clouds hiding seams. In a small separate bottom-right detail show ONE assembled lower feather cluster with stronger orange/gold combustion at tips, so material/fx appearance remains consistent with approved reference. Fine heavy woven cloth grain, irregular gravity/compression folds, subtle maintained wear and a few lightly frayed edges, no beggar rags. Crisp realistic game costume concept with modeling clarity, soft shadows and high fine detail. Sparse clean labels only: FRONT, RIGHT SIDE, BACK, C1, C2, C3, F1, F2, F3; thin non-crossing leader lines. No long paragraphs, logo or watermark. Absolutely do not generate another person or a 3D-render screenshot. Prioritize consistent silhouette and explicit cloth-to-feather layered construction over decorative effects.

Edit this technical turnaround sheet with ONE targeted structural clarification. Preserve the exact established charcoal cloth / three-tier phoenix feather design, text styling, matching scale, material fidelity and RIGHT SIDE and BACK views. Correct the LEFT FRONT view so a modeler cannot mistake this back cape for a closed front poncho: use a very faint plain matte light-gray torso fitting form visible ONLY from shoulder level to upper thigh behind the front opening (no head, no arms, no legs, no clothing, no anatomy details). The form occludes the hanging BACK panels. The actual FRONT coverage consists only of scarf folds around the neck and a SHORT diagonal shawl over anatomical RIGHT shoulder (image left), ending near upper chest on that side. Chest center, abdomen and anatomical LEFT upper torso (image right) are OPEN and reveal the plain neutral fitting form. The long back cloak and feather tail are visible only extending past the right outline (image left) and below the fitting form; do not sew the back cloth into a full front panel. Add a small unobtrusive label 'OPEN FRONT' pointing to the chest opening. Make the front-right shoulder drape consistent with the right-side view: short over shoulder, long cloak hanging BEHIND. Keep the other two views and the structural feather tier callouts visually unchanged, with cloth C1 C2 C3 and F1 F2 F3. No human body, face or extra costume, only an abstract torso fitting volume in the front view to clarify garment topology. All tips and collar remain in frame. Do not introduce rigid armor, extra layers or metal clasps. High resolution modeler construction sheet, three orthographic views of one consistent garment.

Use case: technical costume construction / modeler exploded reference. References: Image1 is the chosen orthographic cloak design, maintain its exact garment silhouette, anatomical RIGHT shoulder bias, charcoal worn heavy textile, and THREE tiers of actual phoenix feathers F1/F2/F3. Image2 is the approved close material/mood reference. Create ONE highly legible high-resolution LANDSCAPE STRUCTURAL CONSTRUCTION SHEET for Blender modeling, not another beauty illustration. Pale neutral background, dark precise linework, realistic sculpted gray/charcoal parts with restrained copper leader lines; no fire bloom. Four clear large panels: A 'EXPLODED ASSEMBLY', B 'ROOT ATTACHMENT / SECTION', C 'CLOTH PATTERNS', D 'FEATHER ANATOMY'. In A show all separated parts of ONE garment in a clean oblique exploded arrangement with dotted matching assembly lines, preserving actual shape: C0 soft load-bearing textile yoke wrapping back neck and right shoulder, open at left front with a concealed fabric tie, no metal buckles; C1 ONE long folded scarf band producing three irregular draped ridges, not three disconnected torus rings and no stiff cylindrical standing collar; C2 continuous INNER BACKING CLOTH from shoulder line to behind the last feather roots, ends well ABOVE terminal feather tips; C3 separate SHORTER asymmetrical outer shoulder shawl, draped on right shoulder with diagonal front edge and upper back overlay, covering the upper feather attachment seam. Below show F1 short coverts (18), F2 medium feathers (14), F3 long tail feathers (10) as three clearly separated STAGGERED ROOT ROWS, fan-shaped rather than concentric rings. Individual feather ribs and free vanes visible. Three narrow B1/B2/B3 reinforced textile mounting tapes are sewn to the OUTSIDE face of C2 at stepped diagonal heights; feather quill roots slide 20–30mm under their tape and are secured by two sewn cloth loops. All roots terminate at a backing/tape, NO floating feathers. Assemble from BODY outward: C0 support, C2 backing, F3 low inner long row, F2 overlapping medium row, F1 upper cover row, then C3 overlay hides F1 root, C1 neck scarf hides yoke and shoulder seam. The panel is not seven full length sheets stacked identically: each part has different actual length. In B show a large side CUTAWAY stair-step shingle overlap with actual fabric layers/tapes/stitches: only each feather ROOT is fixed; its flexible quill and distal vane hang free. F1 covers the upper root/vane of F2, F2 covers F3 roots, C2 ends behind the lowest attachment, while the lowest 35–45cm consists of FREE feather tails, not cloth ending in triangle cuts. Show small exploded root detail with folded tape, two stitch lines and captured quill root. Mark 'FIXED ROOT', 'FREE VANE', '35–45% WIDTH OVERLAP', '20–30 mm INSERT'. In C show THREE flat textile pattern shapes C1 scarf band (unfolded rectangle with dashed fold guides; length approx1.45m, width .32m), C2 irregular asymmetrical backing panel (shoulder-to-hem length approx .90m, width .55m before drape) and C3 short asymmetric shoulder shawl (largest flat dimension .60m, draped depth .35–.50m), plus the compact C0 open neck/shoulder yoke as a small separate inset. Match seam registration marks between C0/C1/C2/C3. No detached arbitrary decorative scraps, no shirt, no full-length fabric feather substitutes. In D show three enlarged real feathers, short/medium/long, and one softly arched feather cross-section: narrow buried ROOT, curved central QUILL, asymmetrical thin VANES with fine grouped BARBS and irregular tiny burnt barbtips. F1 length14–20cm, F2 length24–34cm, F3 length32–52cm; axes curve gently rather than straight spears. Black charcoal organic feather, not metal scales/armor or rubber leaves. A tiny orange tip material swatch is enough; keep all construction clear with glow off. Include a small clear dimensions note '1.73 m CHARACTER / CAPE LENGTH ~1.30 m / SPREAD ~0.68 m' and 'OPEN FRONT'. The exact text strings and C/F/B part IDs matter, other labels concise English only, no long paragraphs. Professional production concept cutaway with plausible garment construction and readable layer ordering, no human face/body, no watermark, no prior Blender model visual reference.

Targeted technical correction to this existing four-panel cloak construction sheet. Preserve its garment design, C0-C3 and F1-F3 labels, all feather anatomy, three tier counts, panel layout, flat-pattern dimensions and rendering quality. Correct ONLY the following structural ambiguities: In PANEL A EXPLODED ASSEMBLY, the continuous inner backing C2 must STOP just 30–50mm below the LOWEST root mounting tape B3, clearly ABOVE the long F3 feather tips. Shorten/remove the excess long exposed backing tail below B3. Show a short dark frayed lower cloth hem under B3; below that hem there must be only individually readable free F3 feather vanes, not a full-length triangular backing sheet extending alongside their tips. Keep B1/B2/B3 mounting tapes attached to C2 and roots aligned to their corresponding tapes. This backing is about .90m shoulder-to-hem, while the whole assembled cape is about1.30m; lowest35–45cm are free feathers. PANEL B section already shows the intended stepped construction; ensure its C2 bottom also ends shortly below B3 with no cloth extending to final tips. In PANEL B replace the misleading explanatory parenthetical text '(= lowest 35–45% of cape length)' with exactly '(no cloth backing below this point)' under 'FREE FEATHER TAILS (35–45 cm)'. Do not state that centimeters equal percentages. Keep the separate '35–45% WIDTH OVERLAP' annotation in the feather overlap inset unchanged: this is a WIDTH overlap measurement, not length. Any extra contextual garment text must not introduce conflicting dimensions. The three feather rows remain attached to B1/B2/B3, not floating. No redesign, no extra plates, no human, no fire effects obscuring construction. Professional accurate modeler reference, correct matching part IDs.

note: Concept modeling references, not existing Blender renders or exact CAD patterns. Part counts/dimensions are authoritative in the guide.
